headline: Meta VP warns: 20 months to rebuild infrastructure for AI agents as queries surge 30x
summary: Meta's VP of Engineering states current enterprise infrastructure, built for humans, is breaking under the 30x surge in agentic AI queries, necessitating a rapid transformation.
details: Meta's VP of Engineering, Barak Yagour, stated at VB Transform 2026 that organizations have "maybe 20 months" to rebuild their infrastructure to meet the demands of agentic AI. He emphasized that current enterprise systems were designed for human interaction, not AI agents.

Yagour highlighted that agentic queries hitting Meta's data systems surged 30x in just six months, a shift that is challenging two decades of established infrastructure assumptions. This rapid growth underscores the urgent need for transformation.

This trend extends beyond Meta; automated internet traffic surpassed human traffic last year, reaching 51% of the total, according to Imperva's 2025 Bad Bot Report. This bot traffic is also growing approximately eight times faster than human traffic.

Yagour identified three core assumptions breaking simultaneously within Meta's infrastructure: capacity, identity, and velocity. These fundamental shifts require a complete rethinking of how systems are designed and managed.

On capacity, Yagour noted that "one engineer used to mean one unit of load," but now one engineer can spawn numerous agents, generating the load of 100,000 users overnight. Meta's solution involves creating agent-aware infrastructure with dynamic controls and cost attribution.

The concept of identity is also challenged, as agents do not fit traditional access control categories for human users or deployed services. Agents make autonomous decisions, requiring new frameworks for authentication and authorization.

Velocity is the third strain; while AI tools like GitHub Copilot write 46% of code rapidly, the subsequent pipeline for building, testing, and deploying remains slow. The speed of code generation by agents doesn't accelerate the entire development cycle.

Data is at the core of this pressure. Meta has already shipped "agentic data apps," leading to 63% of new dashboards being built with this tooling within three months, contributing to the 30x rise in agentic queries.

This growth necessitates robust governance. Yagour warned that "autonomy without governance is nothing but chaos," leading Meta to develop trusted data environments where agents can explore data freely, but all outputs are traced and scrutinized by humans.

Furthermore, sensitive fields are masked, and access requests are evaluated in real-time based on the agent's purpose and permissions. Meta's models are also evolving from correlation to reasoning, demanding comprehensive behavioral histories and real-time data streaming.

headline_marked: [[Google reportedly shifts to Intel EMIB-T]] for 9th-gen TPUs, challenging TSMC's CoWoS dominance
headline: Google reportedly shifts to Intel EMIB-T for 9th-gen TPUs, challenging TSMC's CoWoS dominance
summary: This reported move by Google, a long-standing CoWoS customer, signifies a major shift in advanced packaging strategies for AI and HPC processors, potentially diversifying the supply chain.
details: Google plans to use Intel's EMIB-T packaging for its next-generation TPU, codenamed Humufish, according to SemiAnalysis. This marks a significant departure from TSMC's CoWoS technologies, which have been the industry standard for AI and HPC processors.

TSMC's CoWoS has been the de facto advanced packaging option for nearly all AI and HPC processors. Competing offerings are usually considered secondary solutions, but this reported decision by Google could change that perception.

Google has been a long-standing CoWoS customer for its TPUs, from the Third-Generation to the latest Eighth-Generation. Switching from one advanced packaging technology to another is a complex endeavor, involving numerous changes and unknowns.

Unlike CoWoS, Intel's embedded multi-die interconnect bridge (EMIB) technology does not use interposers. Instead, it relies on tiny embedded silicon bridges within the substrate for high-density die-to-die interconnections, with the rest routed through an inexpensive organic substrate.

EMIB-T enhances EMIB by adding through-silicon vias (TSVs) for vertical power flow and integrating sophisticated metal-insulator-metal (MIM) capacitors and a dedicated ground plane. These improvements are crucial for next-generation AI accelerators that demand cleaner and more power.

Both CoWoS-L and EMIB-T are designed for similar applications, and the choice between them involves factors like interconnect performance, power delivery, scaling beyond large package sizes, and mechanical rigidity. Business considerations such as costs, capacity availability, and supply chain diversification also play a significant role.

While SemiAnalysis suggests EMIB's lack of reticle limit as a key advantage, CoWoS-L also addresses this by replacing monolithic silicon interposers with localized LSI bridges. CoWoS-L's RDL interposer offers superior package-wide routing density compared to EMIB-T's organic substrate.
